title: Luqman's counsel, whole
hookLine: a father's advice to his son (31:12–19)
tomorrow: why would God make people into different tribes at all?

cards: Somebody in every family group chat types in all caps. Surah Luqman ends a father's advice on exactly that. The Qur'an says Luqman was given wisdom, and here he is, not preaching to a crowd, just talking to his own son.
The advice starts with God, then moves through parents and patience and pride, and the very last line is about volume. In Pickthall's words: "Be modest in thy bearing and subdue thy voice."

teach.b: It opens at the top: "O my dear son! Ascribe no partners unto Allah."

teach.h: KINDNESS TO PARENTS, NOT BLIND OBEDIENCE.
teach.b: Then God's own voice breaks in about parents: a mother carries her child "in weakness upon weakness"; be grateful to Me and to your parents.
Even if parents push you to set partners beside God, don't obey that, but keep their company kindly in this world. Back to Luqman.
A deed the weight of a mustard seed, hidden in a rock or in the heavens, God brings it out. "O my dear son! Establish worship," call to good, stop what's wrong, be patient with what comes.
"Turn not thy cheek in scorn toward folk, nor walk with pertness in the land." And then the voice: lower it.
The harshest of voices, the verse ends, is the donkey's bray, a homely picture, and it's right there in the text.
Here's the detail to tell someone tonight: the counsel climbs all the way from God down to the volume of a sentence, and treats both as wisdom.
Now hold this week up beside it. Young men at a cave asking for right conduct. A teacher whose damage hid mercy.
A barefoot man asking for a loosened tongue. A lamp beside the dark. Servants who walk gently.
Luqman would have recognized every one.

how: Luqman's counsel (31:12–19) is a passage Muslim parents and teachers turn to when teaching children manners and faith together; it is read in Arabic and in translation.

o: a wise father's advice to his son in surah 31
a king's letter of law to the people of Saba
a farewell speech given on a mountain top

games.q: the week's passages and their lines — tap the pairs.
p: you are in the holy valley

s: Luqman's counsel ends on how loud you speak
be modest in thy bearing and subdue thy voice (31:19).
the passage says obey your parents in everything
keep their company kindly, but don't obey a push to set partners beside God (31:15).
the counsel is only about worship
it moves through parents, small deeds, patience, pride and a lowered voice.

games.q: your friend's parents push her to give up what she believes about God. by Luqman's surah, what does she still owe them?
o: full obedience: parents come before everything, even this.
kindness and good company in this world, without obeying that push.
nothing at all: she can cut them off for good.
games.why: 31:15 holds both: don't obey a push to set partners beside God, and keep company with them kindly in this world.

practice: Make a small plan for a conversation you're dreading: name what you want from it, and name the moment your voice will start to rise. Then choose what you'll do when it does: a breath, a slower sentence, the same words said lower.
Hold that plan through the sit. And if there's a young person in your life, this is a passage worth reading to them one day.

wordCard.voice: Luqman's counsel: a father's advice in surah 31, from God alone down to the sound of your own voice.

orig.note: Arabic: Luqman, the wise man whose counsel fills surah 31's middle.

carryVoice: Last line of the week: lower your voice, not less said but said lower. A week of whole passages, closed quietly.
